title: Flight Centre says a significant number of customer records may have been accessed in a third-party accommodation booking system
date_note: Both pages give 26 November as the day Flight Centre told the ASX; neither gives an earlier day.
geo_basis: company headquarters (assumed Brisbane; the pages read do not state the city)
summary: Flight Centre told the ASX it detected unusual activity in a third-party accommodation booking system and believes a "significant number" of customer records may have been accessed by unknown persons, per NZ Herald and 1News. Most records contain names and some basic travel information; a "very small percentage" may include limited passport details. No credit card, payment or bank details have been identified as accessed.
plain: Flight Centre says unknown people may have accessed a significant number of customer records held in a third-party accommodation booking system. A very small percentage may include limited passport details.
exec: Flight Centre told the ASX that customer records in a third-party booking system used by several of its brands may have been accessed; it has engaged Mandiant.
action: Flight Centre advises customers to be wary of unexpected emails, calls or messages about bookings, not to click links or open attachments, and not to share personal or payment details.
impact: Flight Centre gave no count of records; it says it will contact affected customers directly. Help Net Security, relaying the ASX statement, says the booking-system vendor is unnamed and Flight Centre has changed authentication keys and credentials.

validation.note: 1News and NZ Herald each report Flight Centre's ASX statement that a significant number of customer records may have been accessed; the ASX announcement itself was not read.

review.note: Compared title, date, status, significant number, passport share, no payment details, Mandiant, advice against 1News and NZ Herald
